newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish yields seen up again at Monday's tender.
newsitem.headline: Polish yields seen up again at Monday's tender.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are expected to attack higher ground at Monday's one billion zloty primary auction in line with a month-long trend, analysts said.
They said investors' bids would total some 800 million zlotys and that the treasury would likely be forced to lower minimum prices by at least one grosz at each maturity.
"Banks will play for further yield increases and minimum prices will likely fall by at least one grosz," said Bartlomiej Kumela, treasury dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.
Analysts said the treasury increased Monday's offer by 300 million zlotys to one billion because of gaps in budget financing and it was more inclined to accept lower prices.
At the last seven primary T-bill tenders the treasury cut the minimum price of the benchmark 52-week bill on average by one grosz per auction to this week's price of 83.50.

Analysts said corporates, which usually stir up demand for the shorter 13- and 26-week bills on offer, may not be active on Monday because of large November tax payments, which include an advance payment for December.

"Shorter paper is basically based on non-banking clients and demand for them is likely to be curbed by the double taxes firms have to pay in November," said Rafal Chodzidlo, senior dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
On Monday the treasury will offer 500 million zlotys of the benchmark paper and 250 million zlotys each of the 13-week and 26-week bills.

Analysts said year-on-year inflation lingering at 19.5 percent in September and October, and waning prospects of its quick slow-down would likely keep yields headed upward for the next several auctions.
This week's lower house of parliament vote on the next year's tax bill, which envisiges a budget deficit larger than the original plan at 2.6 percent, would underpin yields in the longer-term.
Analysts expected foreign investor bids at less than 20 million zlotys for each paper length on Monday as a relatively high zloty and uninspiring fundementals discouraged large-scale entry.

"Foreigners are not likely to bid significant amounts on Monday as the zloty is strong at 2.15 percent from the trading band centre. Things could be different if the zloty was at 1.7 percent," said Piotr Bednarek, senior dealer at ING bank.

The zloty was seen fluctuating in a band between 2.2 percent and 1.9 percent from the parity rate next week with foreign direct investment inflows and importers' orders basically balancing out, analysts said.
"This is a good range for the zloty and deals for both buying and selling may go through the market next week," said Mateusz Bieniek, forex dealer at Societe Generale.

Analysts said the National Bank of Poland singalled this week that if large sums go through the post-trade fixing with the central bank, the daily fixed rate may be significantly different from the market close.
The zloty closed the week at 2.8100 per dollar and at 1.8715 to the mark, or about 2.15 percent from the parity rate.

Call money rates were seen inching up toward 20 percent next week as banks square required positions before the end of the monthly reserve period, but no severe money shortage was expected, analysts said.
"One-day rates are likely to be traded above 19 percent next week, the last in November's average reserve," said Malgorzata Sikora from ING Bank.
On Friday overnight rates closed straddling 19 percent, tomorrow/next around 19.10 and spot/next at 19.40.
